question: What does HTML stand for?
ideal_answer: HTML stands for HyperText Markup Language used to structure web pages.

question: What is the purpose of HTML?
ideal_answer: HTML is used to create and structure content on web pages.

question: What is an HTML tag?
ideal_answer: An HTML tag is a keyword enclosed in angle brackets used to define elements on a webpage.

question: What is the basic structure of an HTML document?
ideal_answer: An HTML document typically contains html, head, and body tags.

question: What does the <head> tag contain?
ideal_answer: The head tag contains metadata such as title, styles, scripts, and meta information.

question: What does the <body> tag contain?
ideal_answer: The body tag contains the visible content of the web page such as text, images, and links.

question: What is the use of the <title> tag?
ideal_answer: The title tag defines the title of the webpage shown in the browser tab.

question: What is an HTML attribute?
ideal_answer: An attribute provides additional information about an HTML element and is written inside the opening tag.

question: What is the difference between an HTML element and a tag?
ideal_answer: A tag defines the start or end of an element, while an element includes the start tag, content, and end tag.

question:
What is the purpose of the

tag?
ideal_answer: The p tag is used to define a paragraph in HTML.

question:
What is the
tag used for?
ideal_answer: The br tag is used to insert a line break in text.

question: What is the purpose of the <a> tag?
ideal_answer: The anchor tag is used to create hyperlinks that link one page to another.

question: What is the tag used for?
ideal_answer: The img tag is used to display images on a webpage.

question: What is the <h1> to <h6> tag used for?
ideal_answer: These tags are used to define headings in HTML from largest to smallest.

question: What is the purpose of the <ul> tag?
ideal_answer: The ul tag is used to create an unordered list.

question: What is the purpose of the <ol> tag?
ideal_answer: The ol tag is used to create an ordered list.

question: What is the <li> tag used for?
ideal_answer: The li tag is used to define list items inside ul or ol lists.

question: What is the purpose of the <div> tag?
ideal_answer: The div tag is used as a container to group HTML elements.

question: What is the purpose of the <span> tag?
ideal_answer: The span tag is an inline container used to style or group small parts of text.

question: What is the difference between <div> and <span>?
ideal_answer: Div is a block-level container while span is an inline container.

question: What is the difference between semantic and non-semantic HTML elements?
ideal_answer: Semantic elements clearly describe their meaning in the browser and to developers, such as header, footer, and article, while non-semantic elements like div and span do not convey meaning about their content.

question: What are semantic HTML tags? Give examples.
ideal_answer: Semantic HTML tags clearly describe the purpose of the content they contain, such as header, footer, section, article, and nav.

question: What is the difference between block-level and inline elements?
ideal_answer: Block-level elements take the full width of the page and start on a new line, while inline elements only take the space required and do not start on a new line.

question: What is the purpose of the alt attribute in images?
ideal_answer: The alt attribute provides alternative text for an image if the image cannot be displayed and also improves accessibility for screen readers.

question: What is the difference between id and class attributes?
ideal_answer: The id attribute uniquely identifies a single element on a page, while the class attribute can be used to group multiple elements for styling or scripting.

question: What is the purpose of the meta tag?
ideal_answer: The meta tag provides metadata about the HTML document such as character set, description, keywords, and viewport settings.

question: What is the purpose of the viewport meta tag?
ideal_answer: The viewport meta tag controls how a webpage is displayed on different screen sizes, especially on mobile devices.

question: What is the difference between HTML and HTML5?
ideal_answer: HTML5 introduced new semantic elements, multimedia support like audio and video tags, and APIs that were not available in earlier versions of HTML.

question: What is the purpose of the form tag in HTML?
ideal_answer: The form tag is used to collect user input and send the data to a server for processing.

question: What is the difference between GET and POST methods in forms?
ideal_answer: GET sends form data in the URL and is used for retrieving data, while POST sends data in the request body and is used for submitting sensitive or large data.

question: What are data attributes in HTML?
ideal_answer: Data attributes allow developers to store custom data directly within HTML elements using attributes that start with data-.

question: What is the purpose of the iframe tag?
ideal_answer: The iframe tag is used to embed another HTML page within the current webpage.

question: What is the difference between local and global attributes?
ideal_answer: Global attributes can be applied to any HTML element, while local attributes are specific to certain HTML elements.

question: What is the purpose of the label tag in forms?
ideal_answer: The label tag defines a label for an input element and improves accessibility by linking text to form controls.

question: What is the difference between section and article tags?
ideal_answer: Section represents a thematic grouping of content, while article represents independent, self-contained content.

question: What is the purpose of the nav tag?
ideal_answer: The nav tag defines a section of the page that contains navigation links.

question: What is the purpose of the figure and figcaption tags?
ideal_answer: The figure tag represents media content such as images or diagrams, and figcaption provides a caption for that content.

question: What is the difference between required and placeholder attributes in input fields?
ideal_answer: The required attribute ensures the user must fill the field before submitting the form, while placeholder provides a hint about the expected input.

question: What is the purpose of the tabindex attribute?
ideal_answer: The tabindex attribute controls the order in which elements receive focus when navigating using the keyboard.

question: What are HTML entities?
ideal_answer: HTML entities are used to display reserved characters like <, >, and & that cannot be written directly in HTML.

question: What is the difference between defer and async attributes in script tags?
ideal_answer: The async attribute loads the script asynchronously and executes it as soon as it is available, while defer loads the script asynchronously but executes it only after the HTML document has been fully parsed.

question: What are web storage APIs in HTML5?
ideal_answer: Web Storage APIs allow browsers to store data locally using localStorage and sessionStorage.

question: What is the difference between localStorage and sessionStorage?
ideal_answer: localStorage stores data permanently until it is manually cleared, while sessionStorage stores data only for the duration of the browser session.

question: What are custom data attributes in HTML?
ideal_answer: Custom data attributes allow developers to store extra information in HTML elements using attributes starting with data-.

question: What is the purpose of the canvas element in HTML5?
ideal_answer: The canvas element is used to draw graphics on a web page using JavaScript.

question: What is the difference between the audio and video tags in HTML5?
ideal_answer: The audio tag is used to embed sound content while the video tag is used to embed video content in a webpage.

question: What is the purpose of the source tag in multimedia elements?
ideal_answer: The source tag specifies multiple media resources for elements like audio and video so the browser can choose a supported format.

question: What is the difference between the <section> and <div> elements?
ideal_answer: Section is a semantic element used to define thematic grouping of content, while div is a generic container with no semantic meaning.

question: What is accessibility in HTML?
ideal_answer: Accessibility ensures that web content is usable by people with disabilities using techniques such as semantic tags, alt text, and ARIA attributes.

question: What are ARIA attributes?
ideal_answer: ARIA attributes are used to improve accessibility by providing additional information to assistive technologies like screen readers.

question: What is the purpose of the picture element?
ideal_answer: The picture element allows developers to specify multiple image sources for responsive images based on screen size or device type.

question: What is the difference between strong and b tags?
ideal_answer: The strong tag indicates important text with semantic meaning, while the b tag only makes text bold without semantic importance.

question: What is the purpose of the noscript tag?
ideal_answer: The noscript tag defines content that is displayed when JavaScript is disabled in the browser.

question: What is the difference between HTML DOM and HTML document?
ideal_answer: The HTML document is the web page itself, while the DOM is a programming interface that represents the document as a tree structure for manipulation by JavaScript.

question: What is the purpose of the preload attribute in media elements?
ideal_answer: The preload attribute specifies whether and how the browser should load media files when the page loads.

question: What does CSS stand for?
ideal_answer: CSS stands for Cascading Style Sheets and is used to style and layout web pages.

question: What is the purpose of CSS?
ideal_answer: CSS is used to control the appearance and layout of HTML elements such as colors, fonts, spacing, and positioning.

question: What are the different types of CSS?
ideal_answer: The three types of CSS are Inline CSS, Internal CSS, and External CSS.

question: What is Inline CSS?
ideal_answer: Inline CSS is applied directly to an HTML element using the style attribute.

question: What is Internal CSS?
ideal_answer: Internal CSS is defined within a style tag inside the head section of an HTML document.

question: What is External CSS?
ideal_answer: External CSS is written in a separate CSS file and linked to an HTML document using the link tag.

question: What is a CSS selector?
ideal_answer: A CSS selector is used to select HTML elements that you want to style.

question: What is the difference between class and id selectors?
ideal_answer: A class selector can be used for multiple elements, while an id selector is used for a unique element.

question: What is the CSS box model?
ideal_answer: The CSS box model consists of content, padding, border, and margin which together define the layout of elements.

question: What is the margin property?
ideal_answer: The margin property controls the space outside an element's border.

question: What is the padding property?
ideal_answer: The padding property controls the space between the content and the border of an element.

question: What is the difference between margin and padding?
ideal_answer: Margin controls space outside the element, while padding controls space inside the element.

question: What is the display property?
ideal_answer: The display property specifies how an HTML element is displayed on the page.

question: What is the difference between block and inline elements?
ideal_answer: Block elements take the full width and start on a new line, while inline elements only take the space needed and stay on the same line.

question: What is the position property in CSS?
ideal_answer: The position property defines how an element is positioned on the page such as static, relative, absolute, fixed, or sticky.

question: What is the color property used for?
ideal_answer: The color property is used to set the color of text in an element.

question: What is the background-color property?
ideal_answer: The background-color property sets the background color of an element.

question: What is the font-size property?
ideal_answer: The font-size property specifies the size of text.

question: What is the text-align property?
ideal_answer: The text-align property is used to align text horizontally within an element.

question: What is the border property?
ideal_answer: The border property is used to define the border around an element including its width, style, and color.

question: What is CSS specificity?
ideal_answer: CSS specificity determines which CSS rule is applied when multiple rules target the same element.

question: What are pseudo-classes in CSS?
ideal_answer: Pseudo-classes define a special state of an element such as hover, active, or focus.

question: What are pseudo-elements in CSS?
ideal_answer: Pseudo-elements are used to style specific parts of an element such as the first letter or first line.

question: What is Flexbox in CSS?
ideal_answer: Flexbox is a layout model used to design flexible and responsive layouts.

question: What is the difference between justify-content and align-items?
ideal_answer: justify-content aligns items horizontally along the main axis while align-items aligns items vertically along the cross axis.

question: What is CSS Grid?
ideal_answer: CSS Grid is a two-dimensional layout system used to create complex layouts using rows and columns.

question: What is the difference between Flexbox and Grid?
ideal_answer: Flexbox is one-dimensional for rows or columns while Grid is two-dimensional for both rows and columns.

question: What is the z-index property?
ideal_answer: The z-index property controls the vertical stacking order of positioned elements.

question: What is the difference between relative and absolute positioning?
ideal_answer: Relative positioning moves an element relative to itself while absolute positioning moves an element relative to its nearest positioned ancestor.

question: What is the overflow property?
ideal_answer: The overflow property controls what happens when content overflows the element's box.

question: What are CSS variables?
ideal_answer: CSS variables are custom properties that store reusable values and are defined using --variable-name.

question: What is the difference between inline-block and block display?
ideal_answer: Block elements take full width while inline-block elements only take required width but allow width and height to be set.

question: What is the opacity property?
ideal_answer: Opacity controls the transparency level of an element.

question: What is the difference between visibility hidden and display none?
ideal_answer: visibility hidden hides the element but keeps its space while display none removes the element from the layout.

question: What are media queries?
ideal_answer: Media queries allow CSS to apply styles depending on device screen size or conditions.

question: What is the float property?
ideal_answer: The float property positions an element to the left or right of its container allowing text to wrap around it.

question: What is the clear property?
ideal_answer: The clear property specifies which sides of floating elements are not allowed to float beside the element.

question: What is a responsive design?
ideal_answer: Responsive design ensures a website adapts to different screen sizes and devices.

question: What is the object-fit property?
ideal_answer: The object-fit property specifies how images or videos fit inside their containers.

question: What is the difference between em and rem units?
ideal_answer: em is relative to the parent element's font size while rem is relative to the root element's font size.

question: What is the difference between CSS preprocessors like Sass and normal CSS?
ideal_answer: CSS preprocessors like Sass provide features such as variables, nesting, and mixins which are not available in normal CSS.

question: What are CSS animations?
ideal_answer: CSS animations allow elements to gradually change styles using keyframes.

question: What is the difference between transition and animation?
ideal_answer: Transitions change styles smoothly between two states while animations allow multiple keyframe stages.

question: What is the will-change property?
ideal_answer: The will-change property hints to the browser which properties will change to optimize performance.

question: What is the difference between min-width, max-width, and width?
ideal_answer: width sets a fixed width while min-width and max-width define the minimum and maximum limits.

question: What is the clip-path property?
ideal_answer: clip-path creates complex shapes by clipping parts of an element.

question: What is the difference between absolute and fixed positioning?
ideal_answer: Absolute positioning is relative to the nearest positioned ancestor while fixed positioning is relative to the viewport.

question: What is a stacking context?
ideal_answer: A stacking context determines how elements are layered and rendered along the z-axis.

question: What is the difference between transform and translate?
ideal_answer: Transform is a property used to apply transformations while translate is a specific transformation function used to move elements.

question: What are CSS filters?
ideal_answer: CSS filters apply graphical effects such as blur, brightness, and contrast to elements.

question: What is the difference between grid-template-columns and grid-auto-columns?
ideal_answer: grid-template-columns defines explicit column sizes while grid-auto-columns sets sizes for automatically created columns.

question: What is the aspect-ratio property?
ideal_answer: The aspect-ratio property defines the proportional relationship between width and height.

question: What is the difference between contain and cover in background-size?
ideal_answer: Contain scales the image to fit within the container while cover fills the container completely even if cropping occurs.

question: What is the difference between inline-flex and flex?
ideal_answer: flex behaves like a block element while inline-flex behaves like an inline element but uses flex layout.

question: What is the purpose of the content property in CSS?
ideal_answer: The content property is used with pseudo-elements like ::before and ::after to insert generated content.

question: What does SQL stand for?
ideal_answer: SQL stands for Structured Query Language and is used to manage and manipulate relational databases.

question: What is a database?
ideal_answer: A database is an organized collection of structured data stored electronically.

question: What is a table in SQL?
ideal_answer: A table is a database object that stores data in rows and columns.

question: What is a primary key?
ideal_answer: A primary key uniquely identifies each record in a table.

question: What is a foreign key?
ideal_answer: A foreign key is a column that creates a relationship between two tables.

question: What is the SELECT statement used for?
ideal_answer: The SELECT statement is used to retrieve data from a database table.

question: What does the WHERE clause do?
ideal_answer: The WHERE clause filters records based on specified conditions.

question: What is the INSERT statement used for?
ideal_answer: The INSERT statement is used to add new records into a table.

question: What is the UPDATE statement used for?
ideal_answer: The UPDATE statement modifies existing records in a table.

question: What is the DELETE statement used for?
ideal_answer: The DELETE statement removes records from a table.

question: What is the difference between DELETE and TRUNCATE?
ideal_answer: DELETE removes specific rows while TRUNCATE removes all rows from a table quickly.

question: What is a NULL value in SQL?
ideal_answer: A NULL value represents missing or unknown data in a table.

question: What is the DISTINCT keyword?
ideal_answer: DISTINCT is used to return unique values from a column.

question: What is ORDER BY used for?
ideal_answer: ORDER BY sorts the result set in ascending or descending order.

question: What is GROUP BY used for?
ideal_answer: GROUP BY groups rows that have the same values in specified columns.

question: What is an index?
ideal_answer: An index improves the speed of data retrieval operations on a table.

question: What is a constraint in SQL?
ideal_answer: Constraints enforce rules on table data to maintain accuracy and integrity.

question: What is the LIMIT clause?
ideal_answer: LIMIT restricts the number of records returned in a query.

question: What is a view?
ideal_answer: A view is a virtual table based on the result of an SQL query.

question: What is the LIKE operator used for?
ideal_answer: The LIKE operator is used for pattern matching in queries.

question: What are SQL joins?
ideal_answer: SQL joins combine rows from two or more tables based on a related column.

question: What is an INNER JOIN?
ideal_answer: INNER JOIN returns records that have matching values in both tables.

question: What is a LEFT JOIN?
ideal_answer: LEFT JOIN returns all records from the left table and matched records from the right table.

question: What is a RIGHT JOIN?
ideal_answer: RIGHT JOIN returns all records from the right table and matched rows from the left table.

question: What is a FULL JOIN?
ideal_answer: FULL JOIN returns all records when there is a match in either table.

question: What are aggregate functions?
ideal_answer: Aggregate functions perform calculations on multiple rows and return a single value.

question: What is the HAVING clause?
ideal_answer: HAVING filters grouped records after the GROUP BY clause.

question: What is a subquery?
ideal_answer: A subquery is a query nested inside another SQL query.

question: What is a UNION operator?
ideal_answer: UNION combines results of two queries and removes duplicate rows.

question: What is UNION ALL?
ideal_answer: UNION ALL combines results of multiple queries including duplicates.

question: What is normalization?
ideal_answer: Normalization is the process of organizing data to reduce redundancy.

question: What is a composite key?
ideal_answer: A composite key is a primary key consisting of multiple columns.

question: What is a self join?
ideal_answer: A self join is a join where a table is joined with itself.

question: What is a correlated subquery?
ideal_answer: A correlated subquery depends on the outer query for its values.

question: What is the difference between CHAR and VARCHAR?
ideal_answer: CHAR stores fixed-length strings while VARCHAR stores variable-length strings.

question: What is a stored procedure?
ideal_answer: A stored procedure is a saved SQL program that can be executed later.

question: What is a trigger?
ideal_answer: A trigger is a database action that automatically executes when a specific event occurs.

question: What is denormalization?
ideal_answer: Denormalization is adding redundant data to improve query performance.

question: What is a transaction?
ideal_answer: A transaction is a sequence of database operations treated as a single unit.

question: What are ACID properties?
ideal_answer: ACID properties ensure reliable database transactions.

question: What is indexing and how does it improve performance?
ideal_answer: Indexing improves database performance by allowing faster data retrieval using indexed columns.

question: What is a clustered index?
ideal_answer: A clustered index determines the physical order of data in a table.

question: What is a non-clustered index?
ideal_answer: A non-clustered index stores a separate structure pointing to table rows.

question: What is query optimization?
ideal_answer: Query optimization improves SQL query performance by selecting efficient execution plans.

question: What is a window function?
ideal_answer: Window functions perform calculations across rows related to the current row.

question: What is a CTE in SQL?
ideal_answer: A Common Table Expression is a temporary result set defined within a query.

question: What is database sharding?
ideal_answer: Sharding splits a database into smaller parts across multiple servers.

question: What is replication?
ideal_answer: Replication copies data from one database server to another.

question: What is partitioning in SQL?
ideal_answer: Partitioning divides a large table into smaller pieces for performance.

question: What is the difference between OLTP and OLAP?
ideal_answer: OLTP handles real-time transactions while OLAP handles analytical queries.

question: What is a materialized view?
ideal_answer: A materialized view stores the result of a query physically for faster access.

question: What is deadlock in SQL?
ideal_answer: A deadlock occurs when two transactions wait for each other to release resources.

question: What is a schema?
ideal_answer: A schema defines the logical structure of a database.

question: What is data warehousing?
ideal_answer: A data warehouse stores large amounts of historical data for analysis.

question: What is indexing strategy?
ideal_answer: Indexing strategy involves choosing appropriate indexes to improve query performance.

question: What is Java?
ideal_answer: Java is a high-level, object-oriented programming language used to build platform-independent applications.

question: What are the main features of Java?
ideal_answer: Java features include object-oriented programming, platform independence, security, robustness, and multithreading.

question: What is JVM?
ideal_answer: JVM stands for Java Virtual Machine and it runs Java bytecode on different platforms.

question: What is JDK?
ideal_answer: JDK stands for Java Development Kit and it provides tools needed to develop Java applications.

question: What is JRE?
ideal_answer: JRE stands for Java Runtime Environment and it provides libraries and JVM required to run Java programs.

question: What is a class in Java?
ideal_answer: A class is a blueprint used to create objects.

question: What is an object?
ideal_answer: An object is an instance of a class that contains data and methods.

question: What is inheritance?
ideal_answer: Inheritance allows one class to acquire properties and methods of another class.

question: What is polymorphism?
ideal_answer: Polymorphism allows methods to perform different tasks based on the object.

question: What is encapsulation?
ideal_answer: Encapsulation is the process of wrapping data and methods into a single unit.

question: What is abstraction?
ideal_answer: Abstraction hides implementation details and shows only essential features.

question: What is a constructor?
ideal_answer: A constructor is a special method used to initialize objects.

question: What is method overloading?
ideal_answer: Method overloading allows multiple methods with the same name but different parameters.

question: What is method overriding?
ideal_answer: Method overriding allows a subclass to provide a specific implementation of a method in the parent class.

question: What is the difference between == and equals()?
ideal_answer: == compares object references while equals() compares object values.

question: What is the main method in Java?
ideal_answer: The main method is the entry point of a Java program.

question: What is a package in Java?
ideal_answer: A package is a namespace used to organize classes and interfaces.

question: What is the final keyword?
ideal_answer: The final keyword prevents modification of variables, methods, or classes.

question: What is a static keyword?
ideal_answer: Static is used for variables and methods that belong to the class rather than objects.

question: What is exception handling?
ideal_answer: Exception handling manages runtime errors using try, catch, and finally blocks.

question: What is the difference between checked and unchecked exceptions?
ideal_answer: Checked exceptions are checked at compile time while unchecked exceptions occur at runtime.

question: What is a thread in Java?
ideal_answer: A thread is a lightweight process that enables concurrent execution.

question: What is synchronization in Java?
ideal_answer: Synchronization controls access to shared resources by multiple threads.

question: What is the difference between ArrayList and LinkedList?
ideal_answer: ArrayList uses a dynamic array while LinkedList uses a doubly linked list.

question: What is the difference between interface and abstract class?
ideal_answer: An interface defines a contract while an abstract class can have both abstract and concrete methods.

question: What is the collection framework?
ideal_answer: The collection framework provides classes and interfaces to store and manipulate groups of objects.

question: What is a HashMap?
ideal_answer: HashMap stores key-value pairs and allows one null key.

question: What is the difference between HashMap and Hashtable?
ideal_answer: HashMap is not synchronized while Hashtable is synchronized.

question: What is the difference between String, StringBuilder, and StringBuffer?
ideal_answer: String is immutable while StringBuilder and StringBuffer are mutable.

question: What is garbage collection?
ideal_answer: Garbage collection automatically removes unused objects from memory.

question: What is the difference between stack and heap memory?
ideal_answer: Stack stores method calls while heap stores objects.

question: What is the transient keyword?
ideal_answer: Transient prevents serialization of variables.

question: What is serialization?
ideal_answer: Serialization converts an object into a byte stream.

question: What is the difference between Comparable and Comparator?
ideal_answer: Comparable provides natural ordering while Comparator allows custom ordering.

question: What is lambda expression?
ideal_answer: Lambda expressions provide a concise way to implement functional interfaces.

question: What is JVM architecture?
ideal_answer: JVM architecture includes class loader, runtime data areas, execution engine, and native interface.

question: What is reflection in Java?
ideal_answer: Reflection allows inspection and modification of classes at runtime.

question: What is the difference between fail-fast and fail-safe iterators?
ideal_answer: Fail-fast iterators throw exceptions when collections are modified while fail-safe iterators operate on a copy.

question: What is dependency injection?
ideal_answer: Dependency injection provides objects with dependencies rather than creating them internally.

question: What is Java Stream API?
ideal_answer: Stream API processes collections of objects in a functional style.

question: What is CompletableFuture?
ideal_answer: CompletableFuture enables asynchronous programming in Java.

question: What is a class loader?
ideal_answer: A class loader loads Java classes dynamically into JVM.

question: What is method reference?
ideal_answer: Method references provide a shorthand notation for lambda expressions.

question: What is immutability in Java?
ideal_answer: Immutable objects cannot change state after creation.

question: What is a marker interface?
ideal_answer: A marker interface indicates special behavior to the JVM without methods.

question: What is the difference between ExecutorService and Thread?
ideal_answer: ExecutorService manages thread pools while Thread represents a single thread.

question: What is a volatile keyword?
ideal_answer: Volatile ensures visibility of changes across threads.

question: What is the difference between shallow copy and deep copy?
ideal_answer: Shallow copy copies references while deep copy duplicates objects.

question: What is a daemon thread?
ideal_answer: A daemon thread runs in the background and stops when the main program exits.

question: What is a memory leak in Java?
ideal_answer: A memory leak occurs when objects are no longer used but not released from memory.

question: What is C programming language?
ideal_answer: C is a general-purpose procedural programming language used for system programming and application development.

question: Who developed C language?
ideal_answer: C was developed by Dennis Ritchie at Bell Labs in 1972.

question: What is a variable in C?
ideal_answer: A variable is a named memory location used to store data.

question: What are basic data types in C?
ideal_answer: Basic data types include int, float, char, and double.

question: What is a pointer?
ideal_answer: A pointer is a variable that stores the address of another variable.

question: What is an array?
ideal_answer: An array is a collection of elements of the same data type stored in contiguous memory.

question: What is a function in C?
ideal_answer: A function is a block of code that performs a specific task.

question: What is the difference between declaration and definition?
ideal_answer: Declaration tells the compiler about the variable while definition allocates memory.

question: What is a structure?
ideal_answer: A structure groups variables of different data types under one name.

question: What is a union?
ideal_answer: A union allows storing different data types in the same memory location.

question: What is recursion?
ideal_answer: Recursion is a function calling itself.

question: What are header files?
ideal_answer: Header files contain function declarations and macros.

question: What is printf()?
ideal_answer: printf() prints formatted output to the console.

question: What is scanf()?
ideal_answer: scanf() reads formatted input from the user.

question: What is a loop?
ideal_answer: A loop executes a block of code repeatedly.

question: What is a constant?
ideal_answer: A constant is a value that cannot be changed during program execution.

question: What is a macro?
ideal_answer: A macro is a preprocessor directive used to define constants or code snippets.

question: What is the sizeof operator?
ideal_answer: sizeof returns the memory size of a variable or data type.

question: What is a null pointer?
ideal_answer: A null pointer points to no valid memory location.

question: What is dynamic memory allocation?
ideal_answer: Dynamic memory allocation allocates memory at runtime using malloc or calloc.

question: What is the difference between malloc and calloc?
ideal_answer: malloc allocates memory without initialization while calloc initializes memory to zero.

question: What is a dangling pointer?
ideal_answer: A dangling pointer refers to memory that has already been freed.

question: What is file handling in C?
ideal_answer: File handling allows reading and writing data to files.

question: What is a function pointer?
ideal_answer: A function pointer stores the address of a function.

question: What is static variable?
ideal_answer: Static variables retain their value between function calls.

question: What is extern keyword?
ideal_answer: Extern allows variables to be accessed across multiple files.

question: What is volatile keyword?
ideal_answer: Volatile tells the compiler that variable value may change unexpectedly.

question: What is pointer arithmetic?
ideal_answer: Pointer arithmetic performs operations like increment or decrement on pointers.
